Tara Gomez (Nimbus): Quick help please — our onboarding flow started seeing 403 then a burst of 429s after ~70s. Logs show 'token_bad' then 'quota_exceeded: per_key'. Demo next week, stuck.
Priya Khatri: Thanks. Which SDK/version and are you routing through a gateway?
Tara Gomez (Nimbus): node-sdk v2.1.4 behind our api-gateway. We issue ephemeral tokens TTL=100s and refresh at ~25s before expiry, but we intentionally keep the prior token for 40s to avoid dropping streams.
Eli Morrison: Keeping prior token that long + gateway multiplexing = likely duplicate distinct auth checks within a short window. That can trigger per_key quota quickly.
Tara Gomez (Nimbus): Snippet from their test run: `HTTP 200 -> ok`, later `HTTP 403 {"error":"token_bad"}` then `HTTP 429 {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota":"per_key"}` after retries.
Priya Khatri: Two fast mitigations: 1) reduce old-token retention to <=5s for a smoke test, 2) add jitter/backoff to retries (>=150ms). We can also apply a temporary per-key relax while you validate.
Tara Gomez (Nimbus): Will try `oldKeep=3s` and backoff 250ms now. Any impact to streams?
Eli Morrison: For long-lived streams, keep the same token for the stream duration and only rotate on new connections. Short keep is fine for request/response flows.
CS Bot: Created ticket CS-9951, labels: onboarding, auth, rate-quota. Temporary per-key relax enabled until 3322228110.
Tara Gomez (Nimbus): Quick test: 8m under load after change — no 403 or 429. Looks promising. Thanks!
Priya Khatri: Great. Action items: Tara to continue ramp and confirm stability; CS to add a short note in onboarding docs about proxy header buffering and token swap window; eng to attach introspection logs to CS-9951.
Eli Morrison: I'll add a reproduce CLI snippet to playbook: `node reproduce-swap.js --ttl 100 --refresh 25 --parallel 2` and a reminder to check NTP on proxies.
Tara Gomez (Nimbus): Copy — will update in 1h after more traffic. :thumbsup:
